shots.vo: Somebody says the weather is depressing. Somebody else says the quarterly results are depressing.
shots.image_prompt: rain running down a tall office window at dusk, city rooftops beyond, an empty chair turned away from a desk, layered detailed composition

shots.vo: A third person, who has not left their flat in nine days and cannot remember why they used to like music, says they are a bit depressed.
shots.image_prompt: a dim apartment interior seen across the room, curtains still drawn, a record player thick with dust, scattered objects, full detailed scene

shots.vo: All three used the same word. Only one of them was describing an illness.
shots.image_prompt: a row of identical white cups along a long diner counter, one of them filled with something black, morning light through the window, detailed interior

shots.vo: Around two hundred and eighty million people are living with that illness. The World Health Organization ranks depressive disorders among the leading causes of disability worldwide.
shots.image_prompt: an immense crowd of small identical human silhouettes packed edge to edge and receding to the horizon

shots.vo: Not among mental illnesses. Among all causes, of any kind.
shots.image_prompt: a long table holding stacks of books of very different heights, one stack towering far above the others, raking light

shots.vo: So it is worth being precise about what the word is supposed to mean.
shots.image_prompt: a magnifying lens resting on a blank open book, strong raking lamp light, detailed still life

shots.vo: The first thing to clear away is that depression is not sadness. Treating it as sadness with the volume turned up gets almost everything wrong.
shots.image_prompt: a small rowing boat on a calm bay dwarfed by a vast dark expanse of water behind it, flat muted landscape

shots.vo: Sadness has an object. You are sad about something, and when the something resolves, the sadness resolves with it. Sadness is also, oddly, useful.
shots.image_prompt: a small figure dwarfed by a single closed door in a tall wall, long shadow raking across a patterned floor

shots.vo: It slows you down. It makes you seek company. It signals to other people that they should be gentle with you.
shots.image_prompt: two seated figures on a bench turned slightly toward each other at dusk, trees and railings behind, full scene

shots.vo: Depression frequently has no object at all. And the symptom clinicians look for first is not sadness. It is anhedonia. The loss of the capacity for pleasure.
shots.image_prompt: a dinner table set for one, a full untouched plate, the chair pushed back, dim evening room, drained grey palette

shots.vo: Anhedonia is a much stranger thing than sadness, and much harder to describe from the outside. Food tastes like it is being explained to you.
shots.image_prompt: a heaped bowl of fruit drawn as bare outlines, colour draining outward into the surrounding still life

shots.vo: Music becomes a sequence of correct notes. You can remember loving something without being able to feel it.
shots.image_prompt: an old record player on a sideboard with the record still turning, an empty armchair beside it, dim quiet room

shots.vo: Some people with severe depression report that they cannot feel sad either. The condition took that as well.
shots.image_prompt: a painter's palette on a workbench with every colour mixed down to the same flat grey, brushes laid beside it

shots.vo: None of this is a modern discovery. Physicians described it as melancholia for two thousand years.
shots.image_prompt: an ancient physician's bench crowded with scrolls, bronze instruments and clay vessels, warm sepia, richly detailed

shots.vo: Albrecht Durer engraved it in fifteen fourteen: a winged figure sitting motionless, surrounded by every instrument of measurement and construction, using none of them.

asset.title: Melencolia I (1514)
asset.author: Albrecht Durer
asset.license: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication

shots.vo: It is one of the most accurate portraits of the condition anybody has made, and it predates the word depression by centuries.
shots.image_prompt: a shelf of ancient bound volumes receding into shadow, one small worn book at the far end catching the light

shots.vo: So if it isn't sadness, what is it? Here is where almost everyone, quite reasonably, reaches for the same sentence. It's a chemical imbalance in the brain.
shots.image_prompt: an anatomical brain illustration pinned to a plain wall, two glass beakers and a bold red painted arrow beside it, warm lamp light

shots.vo: Low serotonin.
shots.image_prompt: one enormous molecular model of connected spheres and rods filling the frame, flat coloured field

shots.vo: That sentence has a history, and the history is not the one you would expect. It did not come out of a laboratory.
shots.image_prompt: a long empty laboratory bench at night, rows of clean glassware, cold blue light, deep perspective

shots.vo: It came, in large part, out of advertising.
shots.image_prompt: a 1960s advertising studio, easels holding blank display boards, drafting tools and warm lamps, detailed interior

shots.vo: Through the late eighties and the nineties, the drugs we now call SSRIs arrived, and with them a campaign to explain them to the public.
shots.image_prompt: dozens of identical pill bottles filling the frame in a tight grid, retro colour, subtle shadows

shots.vo: The explanation had to fit inside a television commercial.
shots.image_prompt: a bulky old television set in a crowded 1960s living room, one simple bright shape glowing on the screen

shots.vo: A chemical imbalance in the brain fits inside a television commercial. It is short, it is mechanical, and it puts the illness somewhere respectable.
shots.image_prompt: an enormous empty billboard on a steel frame against a wide open sky, birds, detailed structure

shots.vo: In the body, rather than in the character.
shots.image_prompt: a wooden artist's mannequin standing on a desk beside an open clock movement and brass gears, warm lamp light

shots.vo: It was a simplification from the beginning, and researchers said so at the time. But it was an extremely good simplification, in the commercial sense, and it escaped.
shots.image_prompt: a paper aeroplane sailing out of a tall open window over rooftops, wide detailed view

shots.vo: In twenty twenty-two, a team led by Joanna Moncrieff published an umbrella review in Molecular Psychiatry.
shots.image_prompt: a towering stack of bound journals under an angled lamp at night, one lying open, detailed still life

shots.vo: A study of studies, gathering the evidence for the serotonin hypothesis across six separate lines of research. They found no consistent evidence that depression is caused by low serotonin.
shots.image_prompt: a long library table with six open books laid in a row all angled toward one open folder at the centre, overhead lamps

shots.vo: The press treated this as a demolition. Inside the field, the reaction was closer to a shrug, and the review itself drew serious methodological criticism.
shots.image_prompt: a wall of bold black rectangular bars and blocks stacked in a dense column, harsh contrast

shots.vo: The simple version had been regarded as inadequate for years. What the review demolished was the commercial, not the science.
shots.image_prompt: workers stripping a billboard, torn paper sheets peeling away from the boards, a ladder leaning against the frame

shots.vo: And here is the part that got mangled almost everywhere, so it is worth saying slowly.
shots.image_prompt: a sheet of paper degraded by repeated copying into abstract grey noise, dense close texture

shots.vo: Depression is not simply low serotonin does not mean antidepressants do not work. Those are two separate questions.
shots.image_prompt: two closed doors side by side in a long corridor, a broken chain lying on the floor between them

shots.vo: Aspirin works on headaches. Headaches are not caused by a lack of aspirin. A drug does not have to reverse a deficiency in order to help.
shots.image_prompt: a single white tablet on a saucer beside a glass of water on a bedside table, soft morning light

shots.vo: If you are taking medication and it is helping you, a paper about serotonin is not a reason to stop.
shots.image_prompt: a hand holding a weekly pill organiser over a kitchen table, calm warm light, detailed domestic scene

shots.vo: So what is actually happening?
shots.image_prompt: a dense exploded arrangement of interlocking gears filling the entire frame, brass and steel

shots.vo: The honest answer is that depression is not one condition with one cause, which is precisely why the single-sentence explanation was so appealing and so wrong.
shots.image_prompt: a dozen ornate keys spread around a single keyhole plate, layered shadows, bold composition

shots.vo: But there are patterns, and they are better described as a system stuck in the wrong mode than as a missing ingredient.
shots.image_prompt: a heavy brass valve wheel turned hard against its stop, rivets and fittings, close detailed crop

shots.vo: The clearest of them is the stress system. The body runs a hormonal cascade through the hypothalamus, the pituitary and the adrenal glands.
shots.image_prompt: three brass vessels mounted one above another joined by copper tubing, liquid descending, workshop wall

shots.vo: It produces cortisol, and then, when the threat has passed, it shuts itself off.
shots.image_prompt: a heavy industrial valve closing on a thick pipe, bolts and fittings, detailed two tone rendering

shots.vo: In a substantial share of depressed patients, the shutting off is impaired. The alarm keeps sounding, quietly, for months.
shots.image_prompt: a large alarm bell on a wall in a dim corridor, vibration lines, deep receding perspective

shots.vo: Cortisol is useful for an afternoon and corrosive over a year.
shots.image_prompt: a rusted iron gate in close up, corrosion eating outward across the bars, flaking paint, weathered texture

shots.vo: Chronic elevation is associated with reduced volume in the hippocampus, the structure that handles memory and helps regulate the very stress response that is wearing it down.
shots.image_prompt: a seahorse shaped form held in fine brass calipers, ornate engraved style, richly detailed

shots.vo: A loop that tightens on itself.
shots.image_prompt: a heavy loop of chain closing into a tightening circle, filling the frame, bold mechanical shapes

shots.vo: The second pattern is in the reward circuitry. Dopamine-carrying pathways running from the ventral tegmental area to the nucleus accumbens, and their conversation with the prefrontal cortex.
shots.image_prompt: a dense network of glowing connected nodes and filaments inside a head silhouette, layered depth

shots.vo: This is the machinery that converts I want that into I am getting up.
shots.image_prompt: a factory conveyor line carrying identical crates past machinery, work stations along its length, warm industrial light

shots.vo: Under sustained stress, that conversion degrades. Notice carefully what this means. It is not that the person wants to get up and lacks the willpower.
shots.image_prompt: a stopped factory conveyor line, crates piled up against a gap in the belt, machinery silent, cold light

shots.vo: It is that the step where wanting turns into doing has stopped working reliably. Anhedonia is that failure, experienced from the inside.
shots.image_prompt: two enormous gears that no longer mesh, a stark gap between their teeth, detailed machinery

shots.vo: The third pattern is plasticity. The brain's capacity to remodel its own connections.
shots.image_prompt: a dense branching neural tree filling the entire frame, fine interlaced glowing lines on dark ground

shots.vo: Depression is associated with a measurable reduction in it, and several treatments that work appear to work by restoring it, over weeks rather than hours.
shots.image_prompt: a wide composition, sparse bare branches on the left growing dense and full toward the right

shots.vo: That timescale is itself a clue. It is the timescale of something being rebuilt, not of a level being topped up.
shots.image_prompt: scaffolding wrapped around a small structure under repair, planks and poles, muted construction palette

shots.vo: The fourth is inflammation. In a subset of patients, and it is a subset, inflammatory markers are elevated.
shots.image_prompt: a dense grid of hundreds of small circles filling the frame, a scattered few glowing warm

shots.vo: Inducing inflammation experimentally in healthy volunteers produces the flat, unmotivated state of depression, along with changes in exactly the reward circuits just described.
shots.image_prompt: a clinical steel tray holding a syringe and small glass vials with a folded white cloth, cold overhead light

shots.vo: Which suggests there are biologically distinct conditions currently wearing the same name.
shots.image_prompt: two different engines on adjacent workshop benches with one blank brass nameplate mounted above them both

shots.vo: Now the consequences. This is where the casual use of the word does the most damage.
shots.image_prompt: a heavy shadow falling across a cluttered desk in low raking light, detailed objects

shots.vo: Depression is not only felt. It measurably degrades the things people are held responsible for.
shots.image_prompt: a worn office desk with a stack of unopened folders, a cold cup of coffee and a stopped clock, dim light, detailed

shots.vo: Concentration, working memory, decision speed and mental flexibility all decline. From the outside, this looks exactly like not trying. Someone misses deadlines.
shots.image_prompt: a grid of squares on paper with many of them heavily crossed through in red, tight crop

shots.vo: Forgets what was agreed. Takes four days to answer an email that would have taken four minutes.
shots.image_prompt: a deep stack of paper envelopes filling the frame with dust settled thickly on the top one

shots.vo: The available explanations are ill and lazy, and the second one requires no imagination at all.
shots.image_prompt: two blank paper tags tied to a worn cardboard folder, harsh contrast lighting, close crop

shots.vo: It does not stay in the head either.
shots.image_prompt: a wooden artist's mannequin seated with one hand resting on its chest, desk lamp, long warm shadow

shots.vo: Depression is associated with higher cardiovascular risk and with worse outcomes for people already managing a physical illness, in ways that lifestyle alone does not account for.
shots.image_prompt: a stethoscope coiled on a folded white coat over the back of a wooden chair, cold window light

shots.vo: And it carries a mortality risk of its own. Untreated depression is among the strongest predictors of suicide there is.
shots.image_prompt: an empty wooden chair alone in a dim room, one shaft of window light falling across worn floorboards, deep shadows, muted palette

shots.vo: The World Health Organization puts the combined economic cost of depression and anxiety at up to a trillion dollars a year in lost productivity.
shots.image_prompt: an enormous tower built from stacked rectangular blocks, muted palette, deep shadows

shots.vo: That figure is usually quoted to make the case for funding treatment. It also quietly describes several hundred million people unable to do work they are otherwise capable of.
shots.image_prompt: an aerial view of row upon row of empty desks across a vast open office, deep flat perspective

shots.vo: Which brings us to the part that is about us, rather than about neurons.
shots.image_prompt: a dense crowd of simplified figures seen from above, one figure standing perfectly still

shots.vo: We have assembled a set of expectations around this illness that we would find absurd applied to any other.
shots.image_prompt: a huge set of weighing scales loaded absurdly unevenly, chains and brass pans, detailed

shots.vo: We ask people whose reward circuitry has stopped converting motivation into action to be more motivated. We recommend exercise to someone who cannot start a shower.
shots.image_prompt: a pair of running shoes standing untouched by a door in a dim cluttered hallway, detailed

shots.vo: We tell them to reach out, and the reaching out costs more than they currently have.
And the strange part is that the advice is not even wrong. Exercise has real evidence behind it.
shots.image_prompt: a folded note left on a kitchen table in morning light, cups and crumbs around it, detailed scene

shots.vo: Behavioural activation, deliberately doing things before you feel like doing them, is one of the better-supported treatments in the field.
shots.image_prompt: a small figure stepping onto a path drawn as a bold ascending line across a wide landscape

shots.vo: The problem was never the content of the advice. It is handing somebody the operating instructions for a machine that is currently broken, and recording that as help delivered.
shots.image_prompt: an old radio opened up on a workbench with its valves and parts laid out in neat rows around it, tools scattered

shots.vo: Then there is the word itself. A word that has to cover both a rainy Tuesday and a disabling illness will, in practice, get calibrated to the rainy Tuesday.
shots.image_prompt: a split composition, a rain streaked window on one side and a long hospital corridor on the other

shots.vo: That is simply how language works. The common meaning wins.
shots.image_prompt: a dense grid of identical blank paper tiles filling the frame with a single tile turned face down

shots.vo: Which means that every time somebody says the real thing out loud, they are arguing with the definition before they even reach the end of the sentence.
shots.image_prompt: a heavy closed dictionary on a lectern in a dim library, one shaft of light falling on it, deep shadow

shots.vo: Depression is not sadness, and it is not a missing chemical.
shots.image_prompt: a raindrop running down a window with a small glass vial standing on the sill beside it, cold light, close crop

shots.vo: It is a set of systems, stress regulation, motivation, plasticity, sometimes immunity, that have settled into a state they cannot leave unaided.
shots.image_prompt: four large overlapping circles in different muted colours forming a layered rosette, bold flat shapes filling the frame

shots.vo: It is common. It is treatable. And it is far more mechanical, and far less voluntary, than the word makes it sound.
shots.image_prompt: a wide sunrise over a flat horizon, bold concentric bands of restrained colour, textured sky

shots.vo: The word is the problem. The people using it about the weather are not.
shots.image_prompt: a single monolithic stone block on a plinth in raking light, deep shadow, monumental composition

shots.vo: But the next time somebody tells you they are depressed, it costs about four seconds to find out which of the two things they mean.
shots.image_prompt: two people sitting across a small cafe table leaning toward each other, warm evening light, other tables behind
